checks: The Jacobian of x=r(z)u multiplies the original r(z)^(d−2)/2 by r(z); conditional u is uniform on [−1,1], so b=su gives the uniform layer. Reversing z=H−Br introduces B dr and integrates to V0=B/d on [0,1] or V0(1−a^d) on [a,1].

The endpoint margins at r=1 and r=a are b−1 and a(b+T), respectively. Their signs give the full, partial and empty ray cases. For a partial ray the upper radius H/(B−b) lies in [a,1]. The integral in units V0 gives the subtracted t on every captured ray, including the fully captured rays. At b=−T the radius interval degenerates and at b=1 the cap occupies the full ray; no mixture has atoms at these nonzero endpoints.

The section parametrization has coarea element dz/s. The variable b=−z/r(z) has derivative −H/(Br(z)^2), reverses endpoints from 1 to −T, and the physical condition clips it to [−s,s]. Thus its section weight is (B/H)r(z)^d db/(2s), and z=−br(z) gives the extra factor with the stated sign and power. For s=0, direct integration gives C0 and M=0, exactly matching the delta layer.

On the compact b interval the first two q derivatives are locally bounded for 0<q<1. Differentiating gives M/C0=−(H/B)e′(a0)/d and the nonnegative second derivative. Since a0 is interior, convexity gives both directions of the minimum criterion. The uniform fixed-interval bounds also justify averaging for unbounded laws of finite slopes without a moment condition on s.

For the full cone the apex margin is H>0, so the integrated energy uses b≤1. Support in [0,T] gives base support in [−T,T], hence this energy equals e(a0). Evenness gives central mass 2v−1 and negative tail mass 1−v. On the symmetric interval Jensen gives integrand average at least one (the zero-mass case is immediate), and on the negative tail its minimum is (1+T/B)^(−d)=t/p0. This includes T=1 and does not require centering.
